claims.text: UK universities are eligible to set up a Leverhulme Research Centre.
The purpose of the centre is outstanding original research aspiring to achieve a step-change in scholarship.
The funding opportunity is for the Leverhulme Centenary Research Centres round.
Previously excluded institutions (Universities of Oxford and Cambridge and Imperial College London) will be eligible to apply in this round.
The Trust aims to encourage new approaches that may establish or reshape a field of study and so transform our understanding of a significant contemporary topic.
Up to £10 million is available for up to 10 years.
Eligible institutions are universities in the UK defined as an institution registered by the Office for Students and which holds its own research degree awarding powers.
A Leverhulme Research Centre may be based at a single university or be a collaboration between multiple institutions.
Collaborative research centres are encouraged.
Each UK university is permitted to submit one application as a principal applicant.
A UK university may act as a partner in multiple proposals led by other universities.
The participation of international institutions is encouraged where relevant.
The Trust invites applications for Leverhulme Research Centres that will not only conduct research of outstanding originality but also aspire to achieve a significant step-change in scholarship.
The Trust has a reputation for encouraging higher-risk research, which is often fundamental or curiosity-driven and multi-disciplinary.
The choice of research topic is left open.
Medical and clinical research are ineligible topics.
The chosen topic should be sufficiently large-scale to support an ambitious but realistic research agenda for up to ten years.
Leverhulme Research Centres should not duplicate existing activity at a comparable scale.
Up to £10 million of funding is available for up to 10 years, with an appropriate mid-term review.
The scheme is open to proposed centres which require less than the maximum £10 million funding and a duration shorter than 10 years.
The funding requested should be proportionate to the centre’s proposed duration.
Research centres will be encouraged to seek additional concurrent support from other funding bodies.
The Trust will not award follow-on funding.
At least 75% of the resources must be used to provide funding for research staff.
Associated research costs can be included up to a maximum of 25% of the total budget.
Institutions hosting a Leverhulme Research Centre will be required to provide office and workspace and other university support.
The Trust does not make awards on a full economic costing basis.
Any increases in costs incurred over the lifetime of Leverhulme Research Centres will need to be managed within the funding awarded.
Prospective applicants should follow their university’s internal selection process.
Once a university has decided on their preferred bid, they should contact Emily Nisbet at [email protected] to gain access to the Grants Management System.
The June 2027 closing date is for the receipt of outline applications.
Invitations for full-stage applications are expected to be made in September.
The deadline for full-stage applications is at the end of the year.
Applications must be submitted by a principal applicant based in a UK university, who will act as Director of the Leverhulme Research Centre.
Details of the proposed wider leadership team should be provided in the centre description.
Applications will be considered via a two-stage process: an outline bid and a detailed proposal.
The outline bid consists of a short form and a five-page description of the proposed centre’s structure and research activity.
The description should include reasons why the research area is important and interesting and suited to the Trust’s funding approach.
The description should include the key research questions to be addressed.
The description should include how the centre will contribute to the general subject area.
The description should include the structure of the centre, whether single or multi-site.
The description should include details of the institutions involved and rationale for their participation.
The description should include brief details of key staff who will be involved and their planned contribution.
The description should include the justification for the choice of the principal applicant and senior staff and their suitability.
The description should include an indication of how the resources might be used over the centre’s duration.
Following the shortlisting of outline bids, those reaching the second stage will be invited to submit a detailed proposal.
Those whose full applications are shortlisted will be invited to interview.
Final decisions are anticipated to be made by the Trust Board at its subsequent board meeting.
The Trust is unable to provide feedback on applications.
